messages:
alice.k: kicking off canary for Teal17b (int4) on cluster-7. initial config: batch_size=16, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch=on. seeing intermittent OOMs during spike tests, looks like memory fragmentation rather than steady leak. collecting traces and coredumps.
ben_p: can you paste the short stack/log when it OOMs? curious if it's KV cache or allocation churn.
tessa: quick log excerpt from node-4 at 1761239958:
```
OOM: CUDA alloc failed at alloc.cu:183
alloc_bytes=134217728
trace: forward -> kv_cache_write -> alloc
available_memory=1.1GiB
```
raj: thanks. pattern matches fragmentation — lots of small allocations during decoding (windowed attention + NPAD). two quick ideas: reduce max_new_tokens default for canary (256->128) and enable windowed generation with KV trimming. Also consider lowering continuous batch_size to 8 for the canary traffic class.
alice.k: tried lowering batch_size to 8 and max_new_tokens to 128 locally; end-to-end bench shows no OOMs for 1k concurrent sims but p50 latency went up ~30ms. quality check passed on our eval prompts.
ben_p: sending a deploy with these toggles + kv_eviction_threshold tweak: 0.75 -> 0.6. deploy-bot: canary deploy queued.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to cluster-7/node-4 at 1761239950 (tags: teal17b-int4-canary-2026-03-21).
tessa: ran offline eval against our prompt suite with max_new_tokens=128; delta in perplexity +3%, rouge stable. falls within acceptable regression window for now.
raj: config snippet I'll try in the runtime for the canary (copy to infra later):
```json
{
  "model": "teal17b-int4",
  "batching": { "max_batch_size": 8, "max_latency_ms": 60 },
  "generation": { "max_new_tokens": 128, "generation_window": 64 },
  "kv": { "eviction_threshold": 0.6, "prefetch": true }
}
```
ben_p: also enabling soft-eviction (graceful KV prune after 75% of sequence) to avoid sudden large frees that fragment.
alice.k: rolling that config to canary now. monitoring memory fragmentation metrics and p99 latency. will keep ref-run with original config for back-to-back comparison.
ben_p: if we still see spikes, next step is to try page-allocator tuning (cudaMallocPool) and enabling compaction after heavy requests.
tessa: FYI I ran a small quality sweep with generation_window=64 vs 128 — negligible change on user-facing metrics but lower tail-memory.
raj: action items: 1) alice.k monitor canary for 1h and post memory profile, 2) ben_p prepare fallback plan to revert to mixed-precision v2 if regressions exceed thresholds, 3) tessa validate longer prompt eval overnight.
alice.k: ack. starting 1h watch now. will post a concise update in this thread when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ben_p: thanks — nice work narrowing frag hypothesis quickly. :thumbsup:
